01 Dorothée Meisner · Researcher of editorial practices

The measurement of the editorial.

Dorothée Meisner knows the feeling: New colleagues work hard. Files are considered finished – and have to be touched again later. After the end of the project, hardly anyone knows how it happened.

"Which procedures work under what conditions – and why?
Explore case ↓Workshop overview

Today, she's investigating this very thing. Cumulative dissertation The doctoral researchers combines historical and sociological digital humanities with data science. Own experience in edition and project coordination shapes her questions.

Why do I care about this as an editor or editor?

If recurring frictions become understandable, training, tool selection and handovers can be better designed. Dorothée wants to learn from experiences that otherwise remain in individual projects together with the edition community.

02

Dorothée works with Git, TEI and own scripts

An archive of decisions.

Dorothée loads repositories, reads edition guidelines and arranges the work packages. For some work data, she arranges a protected research access. Her Python scripts read previous TEI states; it then checks changes itself on text examples and project documents.

A clustering group provides its first candidate for similar processes. Whether these belong together professionally, it decides through comparisons and discussions – not by the label of the procedure.

R1 / Publication repository

The result

Released states. In between, much work can remain invisible.

R2 / hybrid git

Result and path

Publication and editing in the same inventory. Your functions must be kept apart.

R3 / Working repository

Intermediaries

Processing, checks and internal notes. Access may be public or specially protected.

A work package / schematic data

Which makes an additional dimension visible.

Measurements and static table of values

Documents of a fixed package of 40 texts are counted: transcribed, annotated, released after review. The categories overlap; they are not added. A approval can be reopened.

What does Git History show – and what doesn't it show?

Version history documents state changes, not a complete work history. Git stands are traces of previously completed work. Time stamps are not a working time record. A publication import can represent older production. Explanations require comparison designs, dating and, if necessary, interviews and documents.

For discussion

What do we learn from the current result – and what only from the historical states?

03

A completed sub-study / essay in the print

From scan to edition.

After her presentation, Dorothée puts a picture from the print flag of her essay on the table. Her completed OCR/HTR study shows: Better text recognition not only changes the first version. It shifts correction, responsibilities and editorial approval.

1 / Early introduction

Hope was faster than progress.

Expected time gains remained in several investigated projects. Post correction was underestimated. It remained unclear who checks errors and which version is taken over in TEI. Double corrections and re-exports generated rework.

2 / Committed procedures

Recognition and organization learn to do so.

In later stages of their sample Dorothée measures better detection and more stable processes. Regulated postal correction, independent control and reliable TEI integration make the technical profit usable.

3 / To date

Good tools do not prevent every detour.

Two competing corrections, unclear decreases or re-exports that overwrite corrections: such antipatterns can also be found in recent projects.

Schematic processing chain

First hand text

  1. Create transcription
  2. Read back independently
  3. Check and accept corrections
  4. Editing

Schematic processing chain

OCR/HTR initial version

  1. Generate and check detection
  2. Perform postal correction
  3. Independent quality control
  4. Integrate and share TEI
Who proposes, who examines, who decides?

In one project, initial processing and mutual examination alternate in partnership. In another, the final decision remains with a fixed acceptance authority. Git-Diffs and documented reviews prove this distribution in the observed process; they do not explain private motives. Dorothée considers treatment, examination and final decision separately.

"I could see this because these teams have made their work history accessible. I wish more projects would allow research access – or be accompanied from the very beginning."

With her essay, she wants to spread tried and tested procedures. She wants to check whether the established connections also apply to other types of editions with further cases.

For discussion

What organization of correction, approval and TEI integration actually makes better text recognition useful?

04

Conference demo and open research questions

The next upheaval is now underway.

At a conference Dorothée sees an almost autonomous edition pipeline. It is fascinated. But the demonstration shows a successful run, not a reliable long-term operation. In recent repos she looks for changed review sequences, new control tasks and learning opportunities for young editors.

Hypothetical procedure

Classical

People transcribe and annotate. Others examine the proposals; editors decide.

Hypothetical procedure

LLM-supported

A model proposes annotations. People examine the justification and correct it. New tasks arise during systematic testing.

Hypothetical procedure

Agent-shaped

An agent connects several steps. Who controls commits, exceptions and approvals? What errors remain unnoticed over longer runs?

The subject-matter changesDorothée himself conducts research with scripts, TEI analysis and statistics. LLM and agents here are investigated production processes. Their probation and their consequences for qualification are open research questions.

For discussion

Where would you test automation – and where would you like to keep human scientific decision-making authority?

05

Practical insights for the specialist community

Less frustration. Better editions.

Dorothée wants to turn her findings into work tools: a typology of workflows, instructions for tool adjustment and more realistic expectations for correction and training. Comparable values are intended to help teams think, not to put employees on leaderboards.

Four possible wins, even without selection

Introduce: Plan learning phases as your own project task. Quality: Merge corrections to relevant files. Planning: Rework and approvals take into account. Qualification: convey new testing skills and consciously shape routine as a learning space. These tools must prove themselves in further projects.

To do this, she needs more than the well-documented success cases. Broader access and longer-term accompanying research could also refute her assumptions. Efficiency considers them together with quality, available effort and social costs.

For discussion

Which of these findings would improve your own everyday work?

06

The transshipment point / Dorothée stops

A second image in commit history.

In order to understand team changes and continuity, Dorothée tries to arrange the changes according to accounts. Some often appear at night or on weekends, others have longer gaps. She already knows some names from historical team lists.

"Actually, I wanted to explain project practices. Now I could observe individual colleagues."

A comparison with job and career data would be easy to follow. However, no additional work or care obligations can be proven from these timestamps. It arranges a consultation with the data protection officer of the university.

Another question of the same collection

From the project trend to the possible person profile.

The focus of the project is on handovers, reviews and rework. The next link would address individual people and their presumed circumstances.

Before deepening decide.

No individual time profiles are displayed. Dorothée asks: Does my research question need this assignment? Who would be recognizable? Could package sequences or jointly planned interviews answer the same question?

The account assignment is a separate processing step. In small teams, even a renamed account can be easily recognizable.

Watch timestamp→Assign account→Suspicion of circumstances→Evaluate or publish
Not only does the publication change the situation

Even merging and evaluation can be personal. A subsequent aggregation does not undo previous processing. Repository access, methodological significance and legal admissibility are independent questions; the case history does not decide any legal situation.

For discussion

At which concrete Action would you interrupt the investigation? What would a responsible next step be needed?

07

Shaping research interest and protection together

Researching without illuminating.

Dorothée wants to study more working repositorysitories and accompany ongoing projects. Only in this way can individual findings become verifiable experience knowledge. She also wants to give weight to social costs: Who gets learning opportunities? Which job is overlooked in planning? What changes automation in employment and qualifications?

The team that could give them access needs confidential cooperation at the same time. Small groups remain re-identifiable. Only voluntary, well-organised projects would also be a distorted sample. Both cannot be done with a flat-rate "anonymized".

What makes research possible

Better procedures, comprehensible planning, less rework and arguments for good learning and employment conditions.

Dorothée's desire for more access is a legitimate research interest. Without investigation, structural problems can remain invisible.

What workers need to protect

Confidential work spaces, context of own decisions and influence on the use of their traces.

A research interest does not justify a claim to a complete unprotected Git history. Even a project release does not replace any necessary clarification.

What forms would be negotiable?

Curated data levels, time-limited controlled research access or co-planned accompanying research. Prior to sensitive evaluations, the purpose is to clarify sustainable legal basis, employee involvement, safe processing and publication barriers. Consent in the employment context is not an automatic solution. Feedback and contextualisation can be part of an agreement.

For discussion

Which research at our working repositorysitories do we want to enable – on what terms and with whose codecision?

Concepts of this case history
Repository: versioned inventory of files. A working repositorysitory contains editing states; a publication repositorysitory offers released results. A collection can connect both functions.
Git History: received file versions and documented changes. It contains traces of the work, not a complete record of the work process. A commit documents a change; a diff shows differences between states.
Test, editorial review and approval: A test examines a finding. A editorial review is a editorial review. A Z XQ2 is a decision about a ZX Q3. Technical validity alone is not a ZXq4.
